text:
maria: quick check — running into flaky auth + streaming with the Python SDK. using poetry v1.4, httpx 0.24.x, py3.11. when streaming async responses we sometimes get a 401 mid-stream and the client raises CancelledError / RemoteProtocolError. anyone seen this?
chris: have you confirmed token refresh logic? are you using env key or a rotating creds flow? can you paste minimal repro?
maria: using REDWOOD_API_KEY env for now. minimal pattern:
```py
async with Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) as client:
    async for chunk in client.text_stream(model='redwood-1', prompt=prompt):
        process(chunk)
```
we get CancelledError after a few hundred tokens, no obvious pattern.
sahil: two things to try: 1) httpx had a streaming regression around some 0.24 versions — try pinning to 0.23.3 or the latest 0.24.x patch release. 2) if tokens can rotate, make sure rotation isn't happening out-of-band (race).
jen: also check you're not recreating the client per request. persistent client keeps connection and auth header stable; if your env var changes the running client's headers won't auto-update.
alex: for reliability we wrap the request in a retry loop (retries on 429/502/503/504). note: automatic retries don't work for mid-stream failures — we do an outer retry that restarts the stream from a cached prefix.
maria: we don't have a resume helper in the SDK atm — how do you resume without duplicating output?
alex: we cache the tokenized prefix (or last N chars) and call generation again with prompt=prefix+remaining to continue. it's imperfect but avoids re-generating whole thing.
devex-bot: FYI there's an open PR (#412) to add a resumable stream helper & better streaming error classes to the py-sdk — target merge next week.
chris: on typing: if you see mypy complaining about AsyncIterator[str] or missing attributes, ensure typing-extensions is pinned and add type stubs for httpx (e.g., types-httpx) or types-requests if you rely on those. some CI failures are just stubs missing.
sahil: repro tip: use poetry export to lock exact transitive httpx: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt` then `pip install -r reqs.txt` — reproduces patch-level regressions.
maria: thanks — i'll try locking httpx to 0.23.3 and switch to a single long-lived client. will test rotating creds separately and report back.
jen: :thumbsup: ping me if you want a quick PR review, might need a tiny change to the async context-manager usage.
chris: :eyes: good plan.
